items.title: Types of Forces
items.body: Weight \(W=mg\), Normal reaction \(N\), Tension \(T\), Friction \(F\leq\mu N\). Forces are vectors — resolve horizontally and vertically.

items.title: Equilibrium
items.body: A particle is in equilibrium when the resultant force is zero: \(\sum F_x=0\) and \(\sum F_y=0\). Use triangle/polygon of forces.

items.title: Resolving Forces
items.body: Force \(F\) at angle \(\theta\): horizontal component \(F\cos\theta\), vertical component \(F\sin\theta\).

items.title: Friction
items.body: Limiting friction: \(F=\mu N\). When moving: \(F=\mu N\). Static: \(F\leq\mu N\). \(\mu\) is the coefficient of friction.

items.title: Lami's Theorem
items.body: For three concurrent forces in equilibrium: \(\dfrac{F_1}{\sin\alpha}=\dfrac{F_2}{\sin\beta}=\dfrac{F_3}{\sin\gamma}\)

items.title: Inclined Planes
items.body: On slope at angle \(\alpha\): component along slope \(=mg\sin\alpha\), perpendicular \(=mg\cos\alpha\).

body.en: A force is a vector (magnitude + direction). The resultant of forces is found by vector addition; for equilibrium the resultant is zero. Resolve forces into horizontal and vertical components: \(F_x=F\cos\theta\), \(F_y=F\sin\theta\). Friction force satisfies \(F\leq\mu R\); limiting equilibrium: \(F=\mu R\).

label.en: Normal Reaction R = mg cos θ

caption.en: Closed vector triangle of forces in equilibrium: Weight \(W = 20\text{ N}\), Tension \(T\), and Normal reaction \(R\) summing to zero resultant.

body.en:
Normal reaction is perpendicular to the plane: On an inclined plane of angle \(\alpha\), the normal reaction is \(R = mg\cos\alpha\) (if no other perpendicular forces act). Assuming \(R = mg\) on an inclined plane is an instant fatal error.

Gravity components on a slope: Gravity acts vertically downward. Its resolved components are \(mg\sin\alpha\) acting down the slope and \(mg\cos\alpha\) acting perpendicularly into the plane.

Friction is reactive: The friction force obeys \(F \le \mu R\). It only equals \(\mu R\) when motion is impending (limiting equilibrium) or actively occurring. If a system is stationary and not on the verge of slipping, \(F\) balances whatever force opposes it, satisfying \(F < \mu R\).

label.en: Worked example — Resolving forces in equilibrium

body.en:
A particle is in equilibrium under three forces: 10 N acting due East, 8 N acting due North, and a third force \(F\). Find the magnitude and direction of \(F\).

For equilibrium: \(F_x=-10\) N, \(F_y=-8\) N.

\[|F|=\sqrt{100+64}=\sqrt{164}\approx12.8\text{ N},\quad\tan\theta=\frac{8}{10}\Rightarrow\theta=38.7°\text{ W of S}.\]

label.en: Worked example — Friction on an inclined plane

body.en:
A block of mass 5 kg lies on a rough plane inclined at 30° to the horizontal (\(\mu=0.4\), \(g=10\) m/s²). Find the friction force acting when the block is on the point of sliding down.

Normal reaction: \(R=5g\cos30°=50\times\tfrac{\sqrt3}{2}\approx43.3\) N.

Friction (limiting, up the slope): \(F=0.4\times43.3\approx17.3\) N.

Check: Gravity component down slope \(=50\sin30°=25\) N \(>F\), so block would slide — friction acts up slope.

label.en: Worked Example C — Algebraic Structure & Vieta's Root Relations

body.en:
Solve the quadratic equation \( x^2 - 13x + 36 = 0 \) and verify the sum and product of its roots.

Step-by-step Solution:
  1. Factor into binomials: \( (x - 4)(x - 9) = 0 \implies x = 4 \text{ or } x = 9 \).
  2. Check Vieta's formulas: sum \( = 4 + 9 = \mathbf{13} \) and product \( = (4)(9) = \mathbf{36} \).

label.en: Worked Example D — Algebraic Structure & Vieta's Root Relations

body.en:
Solve the quadratic equation \( x^2 - 10x + 25 = 0 \) and verify the sum and product of its roots.

Step-by-step Solution:
  1. Factor into binomials: \( (x - 5)(x - 5) = 0 \implies x = 5 \text{ or } x = 5 \).
  2. Check Vieta's formulas: sum \( = 5 + 5 = \mathbf{10} \) and product \( = (5)(5) = \mathbf{25} \).

question.en: A block of mass \(8\text{ kg}\) rests in limiting equilibrium on a rough plane inclined at \(30^\circ\) to the horizontal. Taking \(g = 9.8\text{ m/s}^2\): (a) calculate the normal reaction \(R\), (b) find the coefficient of friction \(\mu\) between the block and the plane.

solution.en: (a) Resolve perpendicular to the inclined plane: \[R = mg\cos 30^\circ = 8(9.8)\cos 30^\circ = 78.4 \times \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = 39.2\sqrt{3} \approx 67.9\text{ N (3 s.f.)}\] (b) Resolve parallel to the plane. Since the block is in limiting equilibrium on the verge of sliding down, friction \(F = \mu R\) acts up the plane: \[F = mg\sin 30^\circ = 8(9.8)\sin 30^\circ = 78.4 \times 0.5 = 39.2\text{ N}\] Setting \(F = \mu R\): \[\mu = \dfrac{F}{R} = \dfrac{mg\sin 30^\circ}{mg\cos 30^\circ} = \tan 30^\circ = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{3} \approx 0.577\text{ (3 s.f.)}\]

question.en: A small particle of weight \(24\text{ N}\) is held in equilibrium by two light inextensible strings. String \(A\) makes an angle of \(30^\circ\) with the upward vertical, and string \(B\) makes an angle of \(60^\circ\) with the upward vertical. Find the tensions \(T_A\) and \(T_B\) in the two strings.

solution.en:
Notice that the angle between string \(A\) and string \(B\) is \(30^\circ + 60^\circ = 90^\circ\), so the strings are perpendicular.
Resolve horizontally: \[T_A\sin 30^\circ = T_B\sin 60^\circ \Rightarrow T_A(0.5) = T_B\left(\tfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) \Rightarrow T_A = \sqrt{3}T_B\] Resolve vertically: \[T_A\cos 30^\circ + T_B\cos 60^\circ = 24 \Rightarrow T_A\left(\tfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) + T_B(0.5) = 24\] Substitute \(T_A = \sqrt{3}T_B\): \[(\sqrt{3}T_B)\left(\tfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) + 0.5T_B = 24 \Rightarrow \tfrac{3}{2}T_B + \tfrac{1}{2}T_B = 24 \Rightarrow 2T_B = 24 \Rightarrow T_B = 12\text{ N}\] Then: \[T_A = 12\sqrt{3} \approx 20.8\text{ N (3 s.f.)}\]

question.en: [Forces & Equilibrium · Practice 3] If the governing relation for this system is \( g(t) = 5t + 5 \), evaluate \( g(8) \) and find the inverse input \( t \) when \( g(t) = 50 \).

solution.en: Substitute \( t = 8 \): \( g(8) = 5(8) + 5 = \mathbf{45} \). Setting \( 5t + 5 = 50 \) gives \( 5t = 45 \implies t = \mathbf{9} \).

question.en: [Forces & Equilibrium · Practice 4] If the governing relation for this system is \( g(t) = 6t + 6 \), evaluate \( g(10) \) and find the inverse input \( t \) when \( g(t) = 72 \).

solution.en: Substitute \( t = 10 \): \( g(10) = 6(10) + 6 = \mathbf{66} \). Setting \( 6t + 6 = 72 \) gives \( 6t = 66 \implies t = \mathbf{11} \).
